reference: Shuqi Fu, Linhua Jiang, Christopher J. Conselice et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.19318.

title: Seeing Double: The Theory Defying Twin Flares of TDE 2022dbl
abstract: Partial tidal disruption events, in which a star survives a close passage by a supermassive black hole and may be disrupted again on a subsequent encounter, provide a unique probe of supermassive black hole properties and accretion physics. We examine TDE 2022dbl, a partial tidal disruption event candidate that exhibits two separate UV/optical flares, using 11 new optical spectra, updated UV/optical photometry, and a Keck-II/ESI host-galaxy spectrum. We trace the evolution of the prominent blended N III + He II feature across both flares and find that the blend evolves from N III-dominated to He II-dominated emission, which may reflect changing ionization conditions and a declining efficiency of Bowen fluorescence. The two flares show similar thermal evolution and spectral features, supporting a partial-disruption scenario. The second flare exhibits a broader, plateau-like peak, a longer decline timescale, and less extreme line velocities than the first flare. We suggest that these differences arise from the interaction between debris from the second disruption and an accretion disk formed during the first flare. From the host-galaxy velocity dispersion, we infer a black hole mass of $\log_{10}(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot)=6.01\pm0.45$. No third flare has been detected at the expected recurrence epoch, leading us to propose a new interpretation in which a positive-energy kick during ballistic core reformation delays the return of the surviving remnant.
reference: Xinze Guo, Ryan Chornock, Raffaella Margutti et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.18840.

title: Black hole spin-mass correlation and accretion disks at birth stage of dense star clusters
abstract: We review the accretion-driven channel of stellar black-hole growth and spin-up in gaseous star clusters, developed within the framework of our MSCA project "protoBH". Our detailed calculations involving semi-analytic modelling, dynamical and hydrodynamic simulations suggest that the growth and spin-up of initially low-mass stellar black holes is an integral element of the formation process of dense massive star clusters, such as the proto-globular clusters observed at high redshift. The black holes accrete residual gas, remaining from the first star formation event, and form accretion disks generated by gas angular momentum induced by the black-holes' own curved orbits. Assuming initial black hole masses below the pair-instability mass gap $\leq 55\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$, the gap gets populated with black-hole masses growing to $\sim 10^2\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$, and even reaching several hundred solar masses for sufficiently dense and massive proto-clusters. We predict a consistent spin-mass relation with low black hole spins $\lesssim 0.2$ for low black hole masses $\lesssim 20\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$, spanning all intermediate spins for higher masses and saturating to high spins $\gtrsim 0.8$ for high masses $\gtrsim 70\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$. We find evidence in favour of such an accretion-driven subpopulation of black holes in the GWTC-5.0 released by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration.
reference: Zacharias Roupas (2026), arXiv:2610.18505.

title: Multimessenger Constraints on Nuclear Acceleration in Neutrino-Emitting Seyfert Coronae
abstract: High-energy neutrinos from Seyfert galaxies probe particle acceleration near supermassive black holes, but the accelerated nuclear composition remains uncertain. We connect stochastic acceleration to nuclear and radiative cascades to assess nuclear contributions. Acceleration and losses limit the energy per nucleon available to nuclear cascades; without secondary reacceleration, fragmentation cannot raise this scale. For NGC~1068, joint neutrino and gamma-ray constraints depend on the nuclear mixture: helium-dominated injection permits larger nuclear power fractions than the heavier mixtures considered. For the harder candidate {neutrino} spectrum of NGC~7469, the adopted model yields more energetic nuclear cascades, while the source-specific flux selections allow larger nuclear fractions for the heavier mixtures than in NGC~1068. These results show that composition constraints depend on nuclear yields as well as acceleration conditions and available power.
reference: Chengchao Yuan (2026), arXiv:2610.18671.

title: Broadband non-thermal emission predictions based on 3D simulations of supernova explosions within active galactic nuclei jets
abstract: Thermonuclear and core-collapse supernovae are statistically expected to happen within extragalactic jets, as these jets cross the inner regions of their host galaxies, and supernova ejecta-jet interactions can potentially lead to strong non-thermal activity. We model the non-thermal emission from a supernova interacting with a jet on kiloparsec scales, using detailed numerical simulations of the interaction. Using a post-processing method, we applied a non-thermal model of the acceleration and transport of electron and their synchrotron and inverse Compton emissions, simplified and tuned for flexibility and computational speed, to the results of a three-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics simulation of the ejecta of a supernova interacting with an extragalactic jet. For intermediate jet powers, radio, optical and X-ray fluxes from supernova ejecta-jet interactions may be detectable for distances < 100Mpc. The non-thermal luminosity budget and local conditions associated with these interactions could be enough to explain knots seen in kiloparsec scale jets at different energies. These conditions might also be suitable for the production of heavy ultra high-energy cosmic rays, but photon and neutrino generation from hadronic processes would be minor on kiloparsec scales. The leptonic gamma-ray fluxes are modest but might non-negligibly contribute in TeV for the nearest or more powerful jet sources.
reference: B. Longo, V. Bosch-Ramon, M. Perucho et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.18476.

title: A radio counterpart of the local little-red-dot J092359+415736
abstract: Little red dots (LRDs) are compact red sources at z>~4. Broad lines suggest accreting black holes, yet radio and X-ray measurements are usually weak. Local LRDs allow multi-frequency, multi-epoch radio studies that are inaccessible at high redshift. We search archival radio images for a counterpart to the local LRD J092359+415736 at z~0.323, quantify its long-term radio variability, and identify the plausible origin of the radio emission. Flux densities at the optical position are measured in FIRST, LoTSS, RACS, VAST, and VLASS products spanning 0.144-3.0 GHz and 1994-2024. A compact 144 MHz counterpart is detected at 42sigma in LoTSS, coincident with the Gaia position, and is recovered in FIRST, RACS, VAST, and VLASS. LoTSS and ASKAP give a spectral index alpha ~ -0.30 +/- 0.11. The source varies on multiple timescales: FIRST at 1.4 GHz (1994) is a factor of ~2.6 below ASKAP (2021-2024) and below the extrapolated LoTSS-ASKAP spectrum, indicating long-term brightening over 26 yr; the 3 GHz flux density rises by 2.3sigma between VLASS epochs 2.2 and 3.2. A star-formation-only origin would require ~200 Msun/yr, against an unobscured H-alpha upper limit of 3.3 Msun/yr, implying an extreme obscured starburst. Ordinary radio supernovae and tidal disruption events are strongly disfavoured by the luminosity and 30-yr recovery, while refractive scintillation would itself require an ultracompact nuclear emitter. The persistent radio counterpart is best explained by accretion onto the central black hole. Among the three radio-detected local LRDs, this source is intermediate in luminosity and the only one with reported multi-year variability, adding a temporal dimension to the radio diversity of the class.
reference: Tao An, Ruqiu Lin, Ailing Wang (2026), arXiv:2610.17559.

title: MOSS III: MeerKATs view on the galaxy populations in two massive galaxy clusters
abstract: The MeerKAT Observations of the Saraswati Supercluster (MOSS) is an ongoing project attempting to study the radio and optical properties of the core region of the Saraswati supercluster (z = 0.28) and will eventually entail a full survey of the entire supercluster region. Here we use radio catalogs from previous deep pilot MeerKAT L-band (1.28 GHz) observations (angular resolution of 8 arcsec) of the core region of the Saraswati supercluster. The region hosts two galaxy clusters representing distinct environments: The most massive cluster Abell 2631, and the second most massive cluster ZwCl2341, that is significantly more dynamically active. The deep radio catalogs of these clusters were combined with spectroscopic redshifts (mainly from DESI DR1 and SDSS DR16) and optical photometry catalogs of the cluster member galaxy source population. We use these redshifts together with the 1.4GHz MeerKAT flux densities to derive the dust-free star-formation rate (SFR) and evaluate various trends in the radio SFG and AGN galaxy populations. We find that the actively merging cluster ZwCL2341 has an increased star-forming galaxy population compared to A2631 with up to 4 times more star-forming galaxies. When looking at SFG-related radio processes we see s enhanced SF-related activity in ZwCL2341 with SF-related radio processes dominates entirely over AGN-related radio processes. This suggests that dynamically active environments associated with cluster assembly, such as mergers, have enhanced SF radio-activity and increased SFG (both radio and non-radio) galaxy population compared to lesser active systems.
reference: Robert Kincaid, Mark Sargent, Pascale Jablonka et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.19079.

title: The connection between massive galaxies and their dark matter haloes from $z=0.25$ to $z \sim 4$ from the combined COSMOS, XMM-LSS and ECDF-S fields
abstract: Understanding how galaxies populate and grow within dark matter haloes is essential for linking the observed evolution of galaxies to the hierarchical growth of structure. We present a galaxy clustering analysis using optical and near-infrared data from the UltraVISTA and VIDEO surveys covering $9.3$ deg$^2$ across the COSMOS, XMM-LSS and ECDF-S fields, $\sim 5\times$ larger than previous comparable studies, providing sufficient volume to determine the halo occupation of the most massive galaxies to $z\sim 4$. We measure the angular two-point correlation function for stellar-mass-selected galaxies over $0.25<z<4$ and by combining the three fields, we reduce the cosmic variance by a factor of $\sim2$ compared to the individual fields. The stellar-to-halo mass ratio peaks at a halo mass of $M_{h}\approx10^{12} {\rm M}_{\odot}$ and is a maximum at $z\sim 1$. For the most massive galaxies, the peak halo mass ($M_{h}^{\rm peak}$) increases from $z=1\rightarrow 0$, while the peak stellar mass in such haloes remains approximately constant, indicating that at $z<1$ massive galaxy formation becomes less efficient. We also find a steady increase in the satellite fraction since $z\sim 1$, from which we infer that massive halos continue to grow hierarchically while their central galaxies experience suppressed stellar-mass growth. We suggest this is due to the central massive galaxies having their growth controlled by feedback from active galactic nuclei feedback, likely from low-power stochastic radio emission.
reference: Natalia Stylianou, Matt J. Jarvis, Rohan G. Varadaraj et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.19030.

title: How JWST is Revolutionizing Our View of Early Galaxy Formation
abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has been revolutionizing our understanding of early galaxy formation over its first four years of science operations. With un- precedented sensitivity, spatial resolution, and wavelength coverage from the near- to mid-infrared, JWST has enabled astronomers to identify hundreds of star-forming galaxies at redshifts z>~8 (within ~650 million years of the Big Bang) through strong spectral breaks and characterize these galaxies through sensitive spectroscopy. These capabilities have provided new insights into the stellar populations, neutral gas, nebular continuum emission, chemical enrichment, dust content, and ionization conditions of galaxies during cosmic dawn, revealing more numerous and brighter systems than anticipated from pre-JWST models. We discuss the implications of these discoveries for reionization, the buildup of stellar mass and metals, and the evolution of galaxy populations and luminosity functions. JWST is also revealing a new physical picture of early galaxies, characterized by compact, clumpy star formation, high gas fractions, and intense radiation fields. Despite much progress, many open questions remain, including the efficiency, intermittency, and stellar initial mass function (IMF) of early star formation, conditions in the interstellar medium (ISM), masses, and structure of the earliest galaxies, and the topology of reionization. Resolving these open questions will require lensing magnification, sensitive spectroscopy to > 5 micron, including with the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA), exploration to higher redshifts, and larger, more complete samples, helping to clarify how the first galaxies formed and evolved.
reference: Rychard Bouwens (2026), arXiv:2610.18960.

title: Scaling Up: A Global Optical/X-ray Correlation For Reprocessing Across Black Hole Masses
abstract: This study extends the optical/X-ray correlation from black hole low-mass X-ray binaries (XRBs) to active galactic nuclei (AGN), bridging scales from stellar-mass to supermassive black holes (SMBHs). In XRBs, optical emission predominantly originates from the thermal reprocessing of high-energy photons on the surface of the geometrically thin, optically thick accretion disk. The reprocessed optical luminosity follows a power-law relation of the form $L_{V} \propto L_{X}^β a$, with $β\sim 0.5$, where $L_X$ is the X-ray luminosity and the orbital separation $a$ serves as a proxy for the disk size. To test the universality of this relationship across all mass scales, we analyzed quasi-simultaneous X-ray and optical flux data from a sample of XRBs and AGN that have estimates of the radius of the optically emitting disk. To bridge the structural differences between these populations, we utilized the characteristic optical/X-ray time lag derived from reverberation mapping as a physical proxy for the reprocessing radius. Our analysis reveals a tight, global correlation across all black hole masses, described by $\log L_V = 0.48\log L_X + 0.96\log a_R + 6.5$ with a scatter of $\sim 0.20$ dex, where $a_R$ is the reprocessing radius derived from the lag. Incorporating a geometric correction for the disk inclination angle ($\cos i$) slightly reduces this scatter to $0.18$ dex. These results suggest that X-ray reprocessing is scale-invariant across accretion disks, from stellar-mass black holes to SMBHs. This scaling relation provides new constraints for models of X-ray emission regions in accreting black holes.
reference: Changhyun Cho, David M. Russell, Aaryan Sharma et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.17248.

title: Untangling Similarities and Differences in Star Formation Histories Across Cosmological Simulations
abstract: How galaxies assemble depends on processes ranging from small-scale baryonic physics to large-scale cosmological assembly, which are difficult to disentangle with observations alone. Using $\sim$63,000 simulated galaxies from seven cosmological simulations spanning hydrodynamical, semi-analytic, and semi-empirical models, we explore how specific star formation histories (sSFHs) vary across modelling assumptions. Using non-linear dimensionality reduction (UMAP), we find that sSFH shape variation organizes along a few smooth axes in a 2D embedding, broadly corresponding to (1) peak timing, (2) peak sharpness, and (3) subsequent quenching rate. We identify sSFH shapes that many simulations share ("common"), well described to first order by dark matter halo assembly, and a few tied to individual simulations ("unique"), which likely reflect subgrid and parametrization choices such as merger-triggered burst prescriptions. A notable exception is a common population of rapidly quenched galaxies found across most simulations, likely driven by e.g., active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback, that halo assembly alone cannot reproduce. The origin of the most distinctive unique shape, an Illustris-dominated history with an early peak and slow decline, remains unclear, but we test the effects of short-term variability. With a multi-objective auto-encoder neural network, we recover the simulation that a given sSFH is drawn from with $\sim$95\% out-of-sample accuracy; ablation tests indicate this information is embedded in long-timescale sSFH morphology rather than short-term variability. These results provide avenues for theoretical and observational follow-up connecting star formation histories to subgrid physical models.
reference: Alicia M. Savelli, Matthew A. Kustec, Joshua S. Speagle et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.17359.

title: A Quest for Changing-State AGNs
abstract: We use Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) light curves to identify photometrically selected changing-state active galactic nucleus (CSAGN) candidates. We employ unsupervised deep learning and anomaly detection methods to identify unusual patterns of variability in the light curves of 872,228 AGNs with known variability. We find that 8,504 light curves show anomalous behavior. Among these, 682 sources show evidence for two-state photometric behavior during the Gaia DR3 observing baseline. These 682 CSAGN candidates were selected using an automated statistical pattern recognition approach based on Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) to identify sources whose magnitude distributions are consistent with two preferred brightness levels, substantially reducing the need for human visual inspection in selecting the CSAGN candidates. The candidates tend to have fainter absolute magnitudes and lower redshifts than the non-anomalous Gaia variable AGN sample, suggesting that some may be accreting at lower rates. Our approach builds a large candidate sample with less reliance on human visual selection. Follow-up observations of these sources can help identify what drives changing-state transitions and clarify their connection to accretion-disk physics and supermassive black hole (SMBH) fueling.
reference: Kasra Mokhtarpour, Vicki Sarajedini (2026), arXiv:2610.16982.

title: Radiation-Regulated Spherical Accretion with an Inner Accretion Disk
abstract: We develop a theoretical model for radiation-regulated spherical accretion with an inner accretion disk. In our model, the outer accretion flow remains quasi-spherical and optically thick, while the luminosity generated by the inner disk is self-consistently coupled to the accretion rate and irradiates the inflowing gas. By solving the global transonic structure with radiative transfer treated in the diffusion approximation, we investigate how radiation regulates the flow structure and the accretion rate. We find that the luminosity is constrained by a generalized Eddington limit, leading to a saturated accretion rate typically lower than the classical Bondi prediction by orders of magnitude. At sufficiently low densities, the enthalpy flux of the spherical inflow contributes substantially to the emergent luminosity, in which case the inner disk luminosity is reduced and the accretion flow enters an unsaturated state. A criterion is derived to estimate whether the accretion flow is saturated. We further demonstrate the applicability of our model by considering fallback accretion in failed supernova systems. The predicted nearly constant emergent luminosity, constrained by the generalized Eddington limit, provides a possible explanation for the observed luminosity plateau in the failed supernova candidate M31-2014-DS1. The presence of an inner disk also provides sufficient radiation to avoid the under-luminous predictions of a purely spherical fallback model extending down to the central object. Our model provides a framework for studying radiation-regulated accretion flows in systems where low but finite angular momentum leads to the formation of an accretion disk within a larger-scale quasi-spherical inflow.
reference: Cheng-Liang Jiao, Liying Zhu, Xiang-dong Shi et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.16097.

title: Blackbody evolution and circumstellar medium properties of broad-lined H-rich superluminous supernovae
abstract: Broad-lined H-rich superluminous supernovae (SLSNe II) tend to show signs of interaction, including a UV excess compared to a blackbody function. However, a quantitative analysis of the CSM configuration and the UV excess has so far not been performed for most of the literature sample. Additionally, SN 2023gpw showed signs of asymmetry in its peculiar blackbody and spectral evolution, raising the question of whether similar properties can be found in other SLSNe II. We aim to characterize the circumstellar environment of SLSNe II by searching for signs of asymmetry, quantifying the UV excess, and investigating any IR echoes produced by dust. Diversity among SLSNe II is also explored. We fit blackbody functions to the SEDs of SLSNe II to quantify the UV excess luminosity and its evolution. We use this to investigate mass-loss rates required to produce the excess through interaction. We also investigate the line profiles in SLSN II at late times and compare line velocities to the blackbody radius evolution. We examine public WISE IR images and place constraints on IR echoes. We find mass loss rates of $\sim10^{-4}$ to $\sim0.03\, \mathrm{M_\odot}$~yr$^{-1}$ when assuming all interaction luminosity emerges in the UV, i.e., conservative lower limits for the total mass loss rate. Radii calculated from line velocities in late-time spectra are mostly too large for a spherical interaction photosphere, only compatible with the blackbody radius evolution if the CSM is non-spherical with a low filling factor. This is in some cases supported by a mismatch between spectroscopic and blackbody expansion velocities. Considerable diversity is seen in the sample, probably as a result of different viewing angles and CSM masses. WISE images seem too shallow to observe IR echoes in SLSNe II beyond $z\sim0.1$, but in the nearest event, SN 2020jhm, a likely IR echo is detected, suggesting pre-existing dust.
reference: Tuomas Kangas, Takashi Nagao, Uliana Pylypenko et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.16527.

title: Nearly pristine gas in a galaxy 1 billion years after the Big Bang
abstract: Excitation of carbon and oxygen ions is the primary mechanism by which collapsing gas clouds dissipate heat to form new stars. At early cosmic times, in galaxies with chemically pristine gas, many stars are expected to have masses far larger than the mass of our sun due to the deficit in these elements. We searched for ultra-metal-poor galaxies using their spectroscopic absorption signatures in front of bright background quasars, employing the new GHOST high-resolution spectrograph. Here we report the discovery of the first galaxy containing a reservoir of neutral hydrogen gas with metallicity below the ultra-metal-poor threshold: with a measured carbon-to-hydrogen ratio 11,000 times lower than the Sun, it is the most pristine ever found by a factor of four. UMP-DLA-1 is the only known galaxy with measured carbon and oxygen abundances too low to enable efficient formation of stars with solar mass or below. The low metallicity alone therefore guarantees a top-heavy stellar population, providing a direct view of the chemical composition imprinted by massive low-metallicity stars that perished long before the present day: an elevated oxygen-to-carbon ratio. The abundance pattern of UMP-DLA-1 is likely a close representation of the atomic yields of first- or early second-generation stars.
reference: Sarah E. I. Bosman, Frederick B. Davies, Louise Welsh et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.16509.

title: Anisotropic Radiation in Super-Eddington Active Galactic Nuclei: The Responsivity of Broad-Line Regions to Continuum Variability
abstract: Anisotropic ionizing radiation is a natural theoretical expectation for super-Eddington accretion in active galactic nuclei (AGNs), implying that the ionizing flux incident on the broad-line region (BLR) clouds differs from that measured along the observer's line of sight. Reverberation mapping studies have revealed systematically shortened time lags of the broad H$β$ emission line relative to continuum variations in super-Eddington AGNs, a phenomenon that can be naturally interpreted as a consequence of anisotropic ionizing continuum radiation. To further investigate this anisotropy, we perform a systematic analysis of the H$β$ line responsivity, defined as the ratio of the variability amplitude of H$β$ to that of the driving continuum, for both sub- and super-Eddington AGNs. By combining the effective responsivities measured relative to the driving continuum, after correcting for the continuum--emission-line delay, with photoionization calculations, we infer the ionizing radiation field received by their BLRs. We find that, in super-Eddington AGNs, the ionizing flux inferred from the H$β$ responsivity differs significantly from that observed along the line of sight, whereas the two are in closer agreement in sub-Eddington AGNs. These results provide compelling evidence for strong anisotropy of the incident ionizing radiation in super-Eddington AGNs. We conclude by discussing the broader implications of this anisotropy, including its potential relevance to the "little red dots" recently discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope.
reference: Feng-Na Fang, Pu Du, Jian-Min Wang (2026), arXiv:2610.15255.

title: Mapping the Contracting Corona in GS 1354-64 with Insight-HXMT and XRISM: Evolving X-ray Lags and Quenched Reflection across a Complete State Transition
abstract: We present a comprehensive broadband spectro-temporal analysis of the dynamically confirmed Galactic black hole transient GS 1354-64 during its 2025-26 outburst, using near-simultaneous observations from Insight-HXMT and XRISM. The high spectral resolution of the XRISM-Resolve microcalorimeter, coupled with the high-cadence broadband coverage of Insight-HXMT, reveals a dramatic evolution in the inner accretion geometry. During the early hard-intermediate state, the spectrum was dominated by a hot Comptonizing corona accompanied by relativistically broadened reflection features. As the outburst progressed, the corona cooled efficiently, the photon index steepened (Gamma >~ 2.5), and the reflection signatures, including the broad Fe K-alpha emission, were quenched, yielding a featureless, disk-dominated continuum. Concurrently, Type-C quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) evolved from 0.25 Hz to 6.52 Hz. Cross-spectral timing analysis revealed that the broadband X-ray time lags changed from pronounced positive (hard) delays (~160 ms) at low frequencies to near zero as the source softened. However, a statistical analysis incorporating the measurement uncertainties shows that the broadband lags lack a significant monotonic correlation with the QPO frequency, photon index, or fractional rms. Instead, the scattered lag behavior suggests a competition between positive Comptonization delays and negative thermal reverberation. While the spectral softening and QPO acceleration provide strong evidence for a geometric contraction of the corona (whether interpreted via Lense-Thirring precession or the Two-Component Advective Flow (TCAF) paradigm), the broadband timing properties underscore the turbulent and inhomogeneous nature of the inner flow as the advancing Keplerian disk drives the source into the soft state.
reference: Kaushik Chatterjee, Min Wei, Jie Liao et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.15569.

title: Multiphase Analysis of (U)LIRG Nuclear Activity (MAUNA). I. Spatially Resolved Optical Emission-Line Diagnostics
abstract: We present resolved optical integral-field spectroscopy of the 32 luminous and ultraluminous infrared galaxy systems of the Multiphase Analysis of (U)LIRG Nuclear Activity (MAUNA) sample, drawn from the GOALS survey and selected to have JWST/MIRI medium-resolution spectrometer (MRS) observations. The data set combines new Keck/KCWI observations of 10 systems with archival VLT/MUSE cubes for 22 systems, covering H$β$ to [S II] at ~1 arcsecond spatial resolution (~0.9 kpc at the sample median distance). Using the optical [N II]/H$α$ BPT diagram, we find that composite and LINER-like excitation together account for most of the classified area (median fractions 0.44 and 0.26), while Seyfert-like gas covers a median fraction of 0.02 but carries a far larger proportion of the line luminosity where it is present. Both the projected size of the Seyfert-classified region, $R_{\rm Sy}=0.08$-$7.5$ kpc, and its [O III] luminosity increase with the bolometric AGN luminosity, with $R_{\rm Sy}\propto L_{\rm AGN,bol}^{0.54\pm0.18}$, as expected for gas photoionized at a constant ionization parameter. The scatter about the luminosity relation depends on dust opacity: the [O III] luminosity per unit AGN luminosity falls by $1.09\pm0.25$ dex per unit depth of the 9.7 $μ$m silicate absorption feature (Spearman $ρ=-0.60$, $p=0.001$). Optical excitation diagnostics therefore locate AGN-excited gas reliably but systematically underestimate the luminosity the AGN supplies to the host in the most obscured (U)LIRGs.
reference: Justin A. Kader, Vivian U, Marina Bianchin et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.14653.

title: Beyond the Damped Random Walk: Multiband AGN Variability from SDSS to Rubin LSST
abstract: The flux variability of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs) is commonly modeled using the damped random walk (DRW), but increasingly rich multiband time-domain surveys motivate more flexible stochastic models that characterize variability beyond a single timescale and exploit dependence across bands. Multivariate continuous-time autoregressive moving average (MCARMA) processes extend the multivariate DRW to higher-order stochastic dynamics and provide a matrix-valued power spectral density for characterizing marginal variability and cross-band dependence. In a carefully selected Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) Stripe~82 sample, higher-order models are selected for 109 of 134 AGNs (81.3\%), with substantial rather than marginal support in most objects; convergence diagnostics indicate that this fraction is conservative. The fitted models also reveal strong cross-band dependence that generally decreases with wavelength separation. Motivated by this richer structure, we investigate its recoverability under Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) observing conditions. Model-order recovery depends strongly on the underlying stochastic behavior as well as source brightness and observing cadence. Recovery is high across many of the simulated settings, but deteriorates when the characteristic features of higher-order variability become difficult to distinguish from the multivariate DRW. Additional simulations show that this loss of distinguishability can persist over a range of underlying variability behaviors. These results show that stochastic structure beyond the multivariate DRW is prevalent in our selected SDSS sample, while its recoverability with LSST depends on both observational conditions and the form of the underlying stochastic variability. The methodology is implemented in the Python package mcarma.
reference: Izak Schmidlkofer, Zhirui Hu, Weixiang Yu et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.14618.

title: The Population of Type 1 Active Galactic Nuclei in Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument. I. Profile-dependent Measurements of the Low-redshift Sample
abstract: A DESI DR1 analysis of 114,754 type 1 active galactic nuclei at z ≤ 0.9 compares Lorentzian and Gaussian decompositions of broad Balmer profiles, finding systematic differences in line widths, inferred black-hole masses and correlations.
lay_summary: Imagine measuring the speed of a car with two different rulers. The car has not changed, but the answer does because the rulers describe its motion differently. That is roughly what happens when astronomers use different mathematical shapes to describe glowing hydrogen around black holes: the fitted line widths change, and so do the estimated black-hole masses and accretion rates. The study tests just how large that dependence can become in a very large sample.
scientific_summary: A homogeneous DESI DR1 sample of 114,754 Type 1 AGN (z ≤ 0.9) is fitted using either Lorentzian or multi-Gaussian broad Balmer components. The Gaussian prescription generally yields larger broad-Hβ FWHM and virial black-hole mass estimates, alongside lower inferred accretion rates. For [O III] λ5007/narrow-Hβ versus accretion rate, the authors report Spearman rₛ = −0.206 (Lorentzian) and −0.412 (Gaussian).
caveat: Virial masses are model-dependent. Minor discrepancies between coefficients quoted in different sections of the preprint require checking before reuse.
reference: Yao et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.13218v1; accepted to ApJS per authors.

analysis.question: When we decompose the same Type 1 AGN spectrum using different prescriptions for the broad Balmer wings, how stable are the inferred line widths, black-hole masses and correlations with accretion?
analysis.approach: The authors analyze 114,754 Type 1 AGNs at redshift z ≤ 0.9 from DESI DR1. The critical comparison is controlled: broad Balmer emission is represented either by a Lorentzian profile or by multiple Gaussians, while the other major parts of the spectral fitting are kept comparable. The paper also uses machine-learning-assisted refinement in constructing the sample.
findings: The continuum and [O III] luminosity estimates agree fairly closely across the two prescriptions. The differences are not therefore simply a global change to every spectral measurement.

The Gaussian model generally returns a larger FWHM for broad Hβ. Since single-epoch virial mass estimators depend sensitively on line width, the inferred black-hole masses increase and the inferred Eddington ratios decrease.

The rank correlation between [O III] λ5007 / narrow Hβ and accretion rate becomes substantially stronger: Spearman rₛ = −0.412 for the Gaussian prescription, compared with −0.206 for the Lorentzian one. A similar effect is reported for the NLS1 subsample (−0.435 versus −0.259).
Correlations that remain stable under both models are consistent with a continuous sequence of accretion states rather than NLS1s requiring a wholly separate population.
analysis.interpretation: This is a direct caution for studies that infer BLR physics from fitted optical profiles. The decomposition of broad and narrow Hβ is not an innocuous plotting decision: it propagates into FWHM, virial masses, accretion indicators and the apparent strength of correlations. A robust science result ought to survive sensible profile alternatives, or explicitly include that model-choice uncertainty.
analysis.limitations: The alternative line prescriptions are parameterizations, not unique physical reconstructions of the BLR geometry. The stronger correlation alone does not prove that the Gaussian decomposition is physically correct. The numerical findings here are based on the arXiv abstract; inspect the full fitting procedure and selection function before using the reported coefficients in a manuscript.
analysis.relevance: High priority for optical AGN spectroscopy, BLR-profile modeling and any analysis involving Hβ, NLS1 classifications or Baldwin-type trends. A useful next step is to quantify how the choice of profile alters slopes and intrinsic scatter after controlling for luminosity, mass and accretion rate.

title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
abstract: Emission-line galaxies provide key diagnostics of star formation, chemical enrichment, and AGN activity across cosmic time. We present a systematic census of emission-line sources using JWST/NIRCam wide-field slitless spectroscopy (WFSS) from the COSMOS-3D program, which covers a large contiguous area of 0.33 deg$^2$ and provides F444W grism spectroscopy over $3.9$--$5.1\ μ$m. By combining slitless spectroscopy with deep multi-band imaging data, we construct a homogeneous spectroscopic sample of 12,275 objects at redshift 0--9. The typical $3σ$ line-flux limit reaches $3.2\times10^{-18}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}\ cm^{-2}}$. To address source confusion inherent to slitless spectroscopy, we develop a multi-step identification framework that combines information from spectra, images, spectral energy distributions, and spatial distributions. We introduce convolutional neural network and large language model to emulate the human identification process and improve efficiency. The resulting catalog provides spectroscopic redshifts, emission-line measurements, and derived physical properties for all sources. The F444W WFSS enables the detection of multiple emission lines, including primarily [O III], H$α$, He I $\lambda10830$, [S III] $λ\lambda9531,9069$, Pa$β$, Pa$α$, Br$β$, PAH, Br$α$, allowing a continuous census of galaxies across cosmic time. We construct composite spectra in several redshift bins and detect a variety of faint spectral features that are difficult to identify in individual spectra, including higher-order hydrogen recombination lines, CO absorption bands, and [Fe II] lines. This catalog provides a key reference dataset for studies of galaxy evolution and AGN activity, and demonstrates the power of WFSS for constructing large, unbiased spectroscopic samples over wide areas. The full catalog will be publicly available online upon publication.
reference: Shuqi Fu, Zijian Zhang, Danyang Jiang et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.13920.

title: X-Shooter view of planetary nebulae microstructures I: The case of NGC 7009 knots
abstract: The properties of NGC 7009 knots are investigated by employing UV-to-near-infrared data from the X-Shooter spectrograph. These structures belong to the category of low-ionization structures (LISs), which are characterized by enhanced emission from low-ionization species and whose origin remains enigmatic. Our main goal is to conduct the first dedicated spectroscopic study of LISs using X-Shooter, that covers a wide spectral range from the UV to the near-IR, simultaneously. As a pilot study, we focus on NGC 7009 to investigate its ionized, atomic, and molecular gas, aiming to better characterize the physical properties of its LISs and explore their largely unexplored molecular content. The spectrum was processed through the ESO Reflex pipeline, and the physical properties of LISs were derived with the latest version of PyNeb. More than 250 emission lines were detected in the spectra of NGC 7009 LISs, including rare, forbidden transitions from low- ionization species such as Fe+ and Ni+, as well as two transitions from P+, identified here for the first time in LISs. The detection of multiple shock tracers, together with the shock excitation of [Fe II] and [O I], as revealed by emission-line diagnostics, supports the presence of shocks at LISs. The richness of the spectrum allowed us to derive electron temperatures and densities at the LISs using both collisionally excited and optical recombination lines. In the near-IR spectrum of the LISs, nine ro-vibrational H2 emission lines were detected, seven of which were reported here for the first time. These lines were used to construct the H2 excitation diagram, providing new insights into the physical conditions of the nebular gas. The excitation of molecular hydrogen is most likely dominated by collisional processes through shocks.
reference: L. Konstantinou, S. Akras, K. Bouvis et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.13587.

title: The Silk Nebula: A Newly Discovered Giant [OIII] Emission Filament
abstract: We report [O\,\textsc{iii}] narrow-band imaging of an extremely large-scale nebula, the Silk Nebula, discovered by the SWONS (Super Wide-Field [O\,\textsc{iii}] Narrow-band Survey), together with multi-fiber medium-resolution spectroscopic data covering the H$α$, [N\,\textsc{ii}], [S\,\textsc{ii}], and [O\,\textsc{iii}] emission lines, acquired with the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) as part of the Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic Survey of Nebulae (MRS-N). Based on 2,684 high-quality spectra, we measured its physical parameters, including relative line intensities, radial velocities (RVs), and full widths at half-maximum (FWHMs). The [S\,\textsc{ii}]/H$α$ ratio of the nebula significantly exceeds the shock-excitation threshold of 0.4. Its location in BPT diagnostic diagrams and spatial morphology of [O\,\textsc{iii}] both support the optical emission is dominated by shock-heated gas. The oxygen abundance is near solar and spatially uniform, consistent with a shock propagating into the ambient interstellar medium. Because [O\,\textsc{iii}] is the only emission line that clearly traces the nebular morphology, we base our distance estimate exclusively on the [O\,\textsc{iii}] kinematics, obtaining a fiducial distance of $\sim$160 pc. At this distance, the nebula has a physical extent of $\sim$28 pc along the north-south direction. We suggest that the Silk Nebula is a large [O\,\textsc{iii}] filament possibly associated with a supernova remnant, although a diffuse-ionized-gas (DIG) or ionized-bubble origin cannot be ruled out with the present data, and one of the largest angular-scale [O\,\textsc{iii}] emission structures documented to date. Future deep X-ray observations and shock-modeling efforts are required to firmly establish its nature.
reference: Yi-Fei Wu, Songyu Jia, Chao-Jian Wu et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.13329.

title: High Resolution Spectro-Polarimetric Observations of the Optical Filaments surrounding NGC 1275 with ESPaDOnS
abstract: We analyze archival high spectral resolution ESPaDOnS spectropolarimetric observations (R = $λ/Δλ$ = 68000) of three targeted locations within the filamentary nebula surrounding NGC 1275. We present here the analysis of the main filaments emission lines, namely: [NII]$\lambda6584$, H$α$, and [NII]$\lambda6548$, across our three pointings displaying clear detectable emission, with one also showing additional [SII]$\lambda6716$ and [SII]$\lambda6731$ emission line doublet. Using a Markov Chain Monte-Carlo (MCMC) algorithm and thanks to the exceptionally high spectral resolution of the observations, we resolve for the first time each of the emission lines within one of the pointings into a set of three emission components with a remarkable velocity dispersion contrast ($σ_1 \sim 25$ km/s, $σ_2 \sim 90$ km/s and $σ_3 \sim 208$ km/s). We also perform flux ratios of the three detected emission components, which reveal differences in electron density and ionization sources. Consequently, the ESPaDOnS observations appear to reveal for the first time the overlap of an outer quiescent filament and a central turbulent filament likely affected by the AGN activity at a distance of $\sim 6.8''$ ($\sim 2.5$ kpc) from the central BCG. Finally, ESPaDOnS polarimetric data of one of the pointing allows us to confirm an average linear polarization degree of $\sim 0.15-0.14\%$ and an angle of polarization of $5.3\pm25.7^\circ$ for the optical emission of the filaments, as well as polarization dips associated with the H$α$ emission line and its multiple emission components. We interpret these features and measurements as tentative polarization due to dust scattering.
reference: Benjamin Vigneron, Julie Hlavacek-Larrondo, Luca Fabiani et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.13719.

title: A dust-reddened quasar in a [C II]-luminous host at z=6.55
abstract: Most known quasars at $z>6$ were selected through their rest-frame UV emission. Only a small number of reddened quasars have been identified at these redshifts, leaving their nuclear and host-galaxy properties poorly constrained. We present JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy and ALMA band 6 observations of the quasar J1440+0019 at $z=6.5488$, revealing its dust-reddened nature and jointly characterizing its nucleus and host galaxy. The continuum is best described by an SMC-like extinction law with $E(B-V)=0.20\pm0.03$. Three absorption systems detected in N V, Si IV, and C IV are blueshifted by approximately $900$--$3600$ km s$^{-1}$ and likely trace an ionized nuclear outflow. The broad Mg II line and extinction-corrected continuum yield a black-hole mass of $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot)=9.04\pm0.42$, a bolometric luminosity of $L_{\rm bol}\simeq1.1\times10^{47}$ erg s$^{-1}$, and an Eddington ratio of $λ_{\rm Edd}\simeq0.8$. ALMA observations further reveal its host galaxy to be among the most [C II]-luminous known at $z>6$, with $L_{\mathrm{[C II]}}=(7.21\pm0.25)\times10^9 L_\odot$. For a fiducial dust temperature of 47 K and emissivity index $β=1.6$, the dust continuum implies $L_{\rm TIR}=8.9\times10^{12} L_\odot$ and $M_{\rm dust}=4.0\times10^8 M_\odot$. The inferred dynamical mass places J1440+0019 in the region of the $M_{\rm BH}$--$M_{\rm dyn}$ plane occupied by high-redshift blue quasars. These observations reveal a moderately reddened, rapidly accreting quasar in a luminous, dust-rich host during reionization. Its measured nuclear and host-galaxy properties provide an observational reference for identifying and characterizing similar systems in future systematic searches with wide-area infrared surveys.
reference: Daming Yang, Joseph F. Hennawi, Rychard Bouwens et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.13758.

title: Disk Structure May Determine AGN Variability and Explain the Accretion Disk Size Problem: No Broad Line Region Required
abstract: A radiation-magnetohydrodynamic simulation investigates how an asymmetric accretion disk can affect AGN UV–optical variability and continuum time lags.
lay_summary: Scientists often treat a black hole's glowing disk like a fairly flat plate: a flash of X-rays heats it, and different parts respond after predictable delays. This simulation asks what happens if the plate is uneven and turbulent. From one side, the light behaves as expected. From the thicker side, some signals arrive several times later, suggesting that disk structure alone may explain delays that otherwise look puzzling.
scientific_summary: Three-dimensional, multifrequency radiation-MHD simulations of an AGN disk region emitting at 1300–5940 Å show different timing behavior above and below the midplane. UV–optical emission from the thicker side has weak X-ray correlation and continuum lags approximately 3–5 times the simple light-travel time.
caveat: A simulation demonstrating a plausible mechanism—not evidence that the broad-line region never contributes to continuum reverberation.
reference: Secunda, Jiang & Greene (2026), arXiv:2610.12462v1; submitted to ApJ.

analysis.question: Can intrinsic structure and turbulence in an AGN accretion disk produce UV–optical lags larger than light-travel-time predictions, without requiring an extra reverberating contribution?
analysis.approach: The study uses three-dimensional, multi-frequency radiation-magnetohydrodynamic simulations of the disk region emitting at approximately 1300–5940 Å. The simulated turbulent disk develops an asymmetric vertical structure, allowing the authors to compare radiation emerging from its thinner and thicker sides.
findings: The thinner side broadly follows the standard picture: variations in coronal X-ray irradiation correlate with the resulting UV–optical light curves.
On the thicker side, UV–optical changes correlate much less strongly with the X-ray light curve. Continuum lags are approximately 3–5 times longer than the naive light-travel-time expectation.
In the authors' interpretation, the thicker structure absorbs more coronal X-rays, reducing reprocessing farther out and making intrinsic disk fluctuations relatively more important.
The simulation tracks inward propagation of fluctuations, allowing longer inflow-related delays between emission from different disk radii.
analysis.interpretation: A continuum lag is not necessarily a direct geometric ruler. Its measured value can combine irradiation, transfer through the disk and stochastic fluctuations in the emitting material. This offers a possible alternative explanation for the long-lag, apparently oversized-disk problem in AGN continuum reverberation.
analysis.limitations: This is a physically motivated simulation, not a measurement establishing that all AGN disks have the same asymmetry. The title's “No Broad Line Region Required” should not be interpreted as evidence that the BLR never contributes to diffuse continuum emission. The broad applicability of the proposed geometry needs tests across accretion rates, wavelengths and real objects.
analysis.relevance: Important for interpreting AGN variability and reverberation-mapping results. A useful observational test is whether the wavelength dependence and X-ray correlations of lags can distinguish intrinsic-disk propagation from BLR diffuse-continuum contributions.

title: Exploring Case B I: The Footprints of Hidden Radiation Fields in H I Balmer Decrements
abstract: Theory explores how a soft non-ionizing radiation field alters hydrogen Balmer emission relative to Case B recombination and dust-reddening predictions.
lay_summary: Astronomers use the relative brightness of hydrogen's different colors to estimate how much dust blocks the light. That works only if the gas produces those colors in the expected proportions. This paper explores a different possibility: an extra, relatively cool source of radiation can shift those proportions even without extra dust. By looking at several hydrogen lines together, astronomers may be able to tell the two explanations apart.
scientific_summary: Photoexcitation from hydrogen's metastable 2s level by an additional non-ionizing continuum can perturb Case B Balmer ratios. The reported strongest response occurs for approximate blackbody fields with log10(T_eff/K) ~ 3.2–4.2; Hα/Hβ and Hγ/Hβ shift differently from the conventional dust-reddening trajectory.
caveat: The analysis does not establish that this mechanism operates generally in the dense broad-line regions of AGN.
reference: Dehghanian et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.12715v1; submitted to ApJL.

analysis.question: Could a soft, non-ionizing radiation field change the Balmer decrement enough to mimic reddening or reveal an otherwise hidden radiation source?
analysis.approach: The authors explore departures from the usual Case B recombination assumptions by introducing an additional soft radiation continuum. Their proposed mechanism uses photoexcitation out of hydrogen's metastable 2s level, changing level populations and the subsequent radiative cascade. The theoretical predictions are compared with how standard dust reddening moves Hα/Hβ and Hγ/Hβ ratios.
findings: Case B remains a robust baseline for many nebular conditions, but an additional radiation field can alter the Balmer-line ratios.
The strongest modeled effects occur for fields similar to blackbodies with log₁₀(T_eff/K) around 3.2–4.2.
The shifts in Hα/Hβ and Hγ/Hβ do not follow the same trajectory as a simple dust-reddening law. Joint line-ratio measurements may therefore help distinguish the mechanisms.
A nearby cool source could supply the extra continuum even in a spatially unresolved object whose main ionization is provided by hotter sources.
analysis.interpretation: Balmer decrements are often interpreted as extinction tracers. The broader methodological point is that ratios also depend on radiative transfer and atomic-level excitation, so a single assumed intrinsic decrement can import a systematic error into reddening and luminosity estimates.
analysis.limitations: The paper studies a specific proposed excitation channel and does not establish that it dominates in the high-density BLR of an AGN. The applicability of Case B or its departures depends on gas density, optical depth, incident continuum and geometry. An AGN application would require a separate calculation in a realistic BLR regime.
analysis.relevance: Relevant to Hα/Hβ interpretation, optical spectral decomposition and physical conditions in emitting gas. One possible extension is to test how a non-standard intrinsic decrement biases reddening corrections and optical luminosity estimates in AGN samples.

title: A Single Line-Emitter Identified in an Unbiased Search with JWST/NIRSpec: Multi-Object Coronagraphy for Slitless Spectroscopy
abstract: We report the detection of a previously unknown object with a single emission line within the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, using a new JWST NIRSpec technique called Multi-Object Coronagraphy for Slitless Spectroscopy (MOCSS) with the G140M/F100LP observing mode. The MOCSS technique involves opening almost all the shutters on the NIRSpec microshutter array, while simultaneously closing the shutters that lie on top of known low redshift objects, facilitating a wide field slitless spectroscopic search without contamination from bright objects. This observational technique has enabled the detection of a strong emission line in four different dither positions and in two position angles, and thus cannot be artificial. This line is detected at 1.60 $\rm μm$ with a line flux of $[2.5\pm 0.3]\times10^{-18} \rm erg\ s^{-1} cm^{-2}$ and a FWHM of $13.2\pm2.0$Å, and does not correspond to any known source with some of the deepest HST and JWST imaging in existence. Based upon the absence of imaging detection, we place a lower limit on the observed frame equivalent width (EW) of 7620Å on this object, which strongly limits the number of possible lines that this line can be. Given the wavelength, an EW limit that is near the ceiling of expectation, and the lack of other lines in the bandpass, this line cannot be easily explained by [OII] at $z=3.29$, [OIII] at $z=2.20$, H$α$ at $z=1.44$, and Ly$α$ at $z=12.16$. We discuss possible AGN and transient phenomena that could explain the finding.
reference: Mason S. Huberty, Claudia Scarlata, Matthew J. Hayes et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.12553.

title: Changing-look Active Galactic Nuclei from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument. VII. Testing Disk-Corona Diagnostics with eROSITA
abstract: A comparison of DESI changing-look AGN, matched control sources and eROSITA X-ray data questions whether a proposed optical/X-ray spectral relation uniquely traces accretion-state transitions.
lay_summary: Imagine deciding how fast a runner moves by comparing two numbers that both secretly contain the same stopwatch reading. The numbers will look connected, even if the runner's behavior has not actually changed. This paper finds a similar trap in a proposed diagnostic of changing-look black holes. Depending on how the accretion rate is estimated, an apparent relationship can weaken or even reverse.
scientific_summary: DESI changing-look AGN and eROSITA-matched control AGN show that the α_OX–Eddington-ratio relation is not unique to changing-look sources. Its apparent trend is strongly shaped by shared luminosity terms and covariances; using an X-ray-derived Eddington-ratio estimator can reverse the trend's sign.
caveat: The analysis cautions against inferring disk–corona state transitions solely from correlated estimators; independent accretion indicators are needed.
reference: Guo et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.10331v1; accepted to MNRAS per authors.

analysis.question: Does a proposed V-shaped relation between the UV-to-X-ray spectral slope α_OX and Eddington ratio uniquely diagnose state transitions in changing-look AGNs?
analysis.approach: The authors compare DESI-selected changing-look AGNs with control AGN samples matched to eROSITA X-ray data. They test the dependence of α_OX on different Eddington-ratio estimators and examine whether luminosities shared by both axes can create mathematical covariance. They also consider an effective X-ray photon index derived from eROSITA band fluxes.
findings: A positive α_OX correlation with an optical-continuum-based Eddington ratio is also visible in matched AGNs without changing-look behavior; the association is not unique to CL-AGN.

For the main broad-Hα sample, the observed structure is largely attributable to the known α_OX dependence on UV luminosity and to covariance among L_2500, black-hole mass and the optical accretion estimator.
Replacing the optical estimator with an X-ray-based Eddington ratio can reverse the sign of the relation, because the X-ray luminosity enters the two plotted variables in opposite directions.

The eROSITA effective photon index shows a weak positive association with the X-ray-independent optical Eddington ratio, but the hard-band trend is sensitive to statistical assumptions and does not isolate coronal softening.
analysis.interpretation: The paper is primarily a demonstration of the difference between an observed correlation and a physical state-transition diagnostic. Before invoking a disk–corona transition, one must ensure that the derived quantities on the plot are independent enough to support the inference.
analysis.limitations: This analysis does not demonstrate that changing-look AGNs lack physical accretion-state changes. It challenges the uniqueness and interpretation of one family of diagnostics. More direct X-ray spectroscopy, independent accretion-rate estimates and robust covariance modeling remain needed.
analysis.relevance: Useful for AGN variability studies and for designing statistically defensible correlations between spectroscopic quantities and accretion indicators. In follow-up analysis, construct null models that explicitly include common luminosity terms and selection effects.

title: Widespread steep X-ray spectra of luminous $z\simeq5.85-7.5$ quasars and their implications for future X-ray surveys
abstract: Luminous quasars (QSOs) at the Epoch of Reionization (EoR, $z\gtrsim6$) host billion-solar-mass black holes assembled within the first Gyr of cosmic time. Their X-ray emission probes the innermost accreting regions and constrains the physical state of the corona during early supermassive black hole (SMBH) growth. Previous results from the HYPerluminous quasars at the Epoch of ReionizatION (HYPERION) sample of $z \gtrsim 6$ QSOs, powered by the most rapidly accreted SMBHs, suggested a link between X-ray spectral slope and long-term growth efficiency. We test whether the steep X-ray spectra of luminous z>6 QSOs are a general property of early SMBH growth or a peculiarity of the most efficiently grown SMBHs, using a sample extended mainly to the lowest growth efficiencies. We analysed the largest and most X-ray sensitive sample of 28 luminous QSOs at $z \simeq 5.85-7.56$ (26 used in the correlation analysis), combining HYPERION targets, luminous non-HYPERION sources, and QSOs powered by moderately accreting SMBHs newly observed in our XMM-Newton Large Programme. We re-derived black hole masses and growth indicators for the entire sample homogeneously, incorporating the latest JWST-based spectroscopic measurements to ensure the most consistent and high-quality characterization across all targets. We found no statistically significant correlation between coronal spectral parameters and BH growth indicators: luminous $z \gtrsim 6$ QSOs systematically show steep X-ray continua, with high photon indices and/or low high-energy cutoffs, consistent with cold coronae, possibly linked to rapid accretion. Finally, if steep X-ray slopes are common among early AGN, they may significantly reduce count rates, at fixed intrinsic luminosity, in future surveys of the EoR, affecting the detectability of steep-spectrum X-ray sources and thus the census of the early AGN population.
reference: A. Tortosa, L. Zappacosta, E. Piconcelli et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.10522.

title: Cosmic Duets II. Growth and accretion in Gaia Multi-Peak dual AGN at Cosmic Noon
abstract: We present the first statistical characterization of the physical properties of Cosmic Duets: dual AGN in the redshift range 0.5 $\leq$ z $\leq$ 3.0 with projected separations of 1-7 kpc, corresponding to systems in which both AGN are expected to reside within the same merger remnant. We analyze the largest homogeneous sample currently available, consisting of 30 spectroscopically confirmed Cosmic Duets selected via the Gaia Multi-Peak technique. Using rest-frame UV-to-optical integral-field spectroscopy for all targets, primarily with VLT/MUSE, VLT/ERIS, and Keck/OSIRIS, we spatially resolve the two AGN components and extract separate spectra for each system. We decompose the continuum, emission lines, and Fe II complexes through spectral fitting. We derive black hole masses of log($M_{BH}/M_{sun}$) ~ 7.4-10.1 and bolometric luminosities of log($L_{bol}/erg s^{-1}$) ~ 44.8-47.2, consistent with those of single AGN at similar redshifts. We finally carry out the first comparison of dual AGN properties with semi-analytical models and hydrodynamical simulations, including L-GalaxiesBH and Astrid. Astrid provides a closer match to the observed black-hole mass-ratio distribution, but its selected systems are predominantly at lower redshifts, resulting in lower bolometric luminosities at fixed G-band magnitude. L-GalaxiesBH perfectly reproduce the observed parameter space, but it predicts more heterogeneous pairs, with higher primary-bolometric luminosity, lower-mass secondary SMBHs, and higher Eddington ratios, resulting in an excess of near-Eddington accreting AGN due to its adopted accretion prescription. Our results suggest that, in GMP-selected systems, secondary SMBH growth is more efficient than predicted by current models, leading to more comparable black-hole masses and accretion power between the two components.
reference: M. Scialpi, F. Mannucci, D. Izquierdo-Villalba et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.10687.

title: Wind-Fed Magnetic Flux and the Emergence of X-ray Coronae in Active Galactic Nuclei
abstract: We propose a scenario for the onset of radiatively efficient Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) in which circumnuclear stellar and supernova-driven winds supply mass and partially ordered magnetic flux to a compact disk reservoir around a supermassive black hole. A coherent poloidal component surviving advection to small radii strengthens inward, lowering the gas plasma beta until mean Maxwell stresses overtake MRI turbulence, compress the disk vertically, and open a magnetically dominated wedge above it. Within a quasi-force-free description of this wedge, the field self-organizes toward a critical twist at which the net radial transport changes sign, defining a magnetic saturation radius $r_c\sim10\,r_g$. The magnetic squeezing of the disk fixes the pressure balance at the interface between the disk and wedge, confining the accumulated flux at $r_c$: flux advected toward this boundary is preferentially shed, fixing $B_r\propto r^{-2}$ in the interior. From the field topology alone we then derive a normalized saturation flux $φ\sim 50$, consistent with the MAD plateau of GRMHD simulations. The resulting compact, time-dependent saturation region is a natural candidate for the AGN X-ray corona, being collisionless, magnetized, and, at high compactness, plausibly pair-rich, with hadronic pair injection providing a conditional additional channel. Its size, variability, and spectral hardness are controlled by $r_c$, the compactness, and the magnetization. We connect these scalings to observed coronal sizes, variability, and the power partition between the corona and jet. We further propose that Little Red and Blue Dots could represent a disk-reservoir phase preceding luminous AGN activity.
reference: Rostom Mbarek (2026), arXiv:2610.10681.

title: Pushing Variability Searches to Extreme Dwarf Galaxies with the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Data Preview 2
abstract: Rubin Data Preview 2 time-domain data are used to search for variability among extreme dwarf galaxies and possible accreting intermediate-mass black holes.
lay_summary: Tiny galaxies might hide smaller black holes, but it is hard to spot them when they are feeding. One clue is that the galaxy's center flickers over time. Scientists used early Rubin Observatory observations to monitor tens of thousands of very small galaxies. They found seven promising variable sources—but most still need more work before anyone can say a black hole is responsible.
scientific_summary: Rubin DP2 light curves (2025-04-25 to 2026-01-06) were examined for roughly 62,000 galaxies with stellar mass below 10⁸ M☉. Seven variable candidates were selected: two are previously known AGN, three resemble supernovae, and two remain unclassified. The apparent variable fraction for i < 24 is 6.8 (+3.1/−2.1) × 10⁻⁴.
caveat: Variability candidates are not automatically AGN detections; spectroscopy is required for confirmation.

analysis.question: Can early Rubin Observatory time-domain imaging find variability in extreme dwarf galaxies and identify candidates for intermediate-mass black-hole accretion?
analysis.approach: The team analyzes difference-imaging light curves in the ELAIS-S1 field from Rubin Data Preview 2, spanning 25 April 2025 to 6 January 2026. They apply single-band and cross-band variability criteria to roughly 62,000 galaxies with stellar masses below 10^8 solar masses and available archival multiwavelength context.
findings: Seven variable extreme-dwarf-galaxy candidates are selected. All are brighter than i = 24 and lie at redshift z < 0.3.
Two of the seven are previously known AGNs, three have variability patterns more consistent with supernovae, and two remain unclassified.
For the magnitude-limited subset, the reported apparent variable fraction is 6.8^(+3.1)_(-2.1) × 10^−4.
Relative to a magnitude-matched sample of more massive galaxies selected in the same way, the variable fraction is comparable or lower by at most approximately a factor of three.
analysis.interpretation: The demonstration is more about the feasibility and selection function of variability-based searches than about a measured black-hole occupation fraction. Rubin's cadence and survey area may make it possible to build a much larger sample of faint variable nuclei.
analysis.limitations: Photometric variability is not an AGN confirmation: supernovae and other transients can produce similar signals. The selection threshold, detection completeness and observing baseline strongly affect the observed fraction. Spectroscopic follow-up is essential to establish the identity and redshift of individual candidates.
analysis.relevance: Directly useful for preparing LSST variability-selection strategies, prioritizing spectroscopic follow-up and studying the interface between time-domain photometry and AGN identification. An obvious next step is to optimize when to request spectra based on variability strength and classification uncertainty.

title: First uGMRT Constraints on Rotation Measure in the Radio-Quiet Seyfert Galaxy NGC 4235
abstract: We present a multi-frequency polarimetric study of the radio-quiet Seyfert galaxy NGC 4235 using the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT), aimed at constraining the Faraday rotation properties of its kpc-scale radio emission. This marks the first-ever analysis of polarization across two frequency bands of the uGMRT and the first constraints on rotation measure (RM) at lower frequencies for a weak radio source (17.1$\pm$1.7 mJy at 1.3 GHz, 27.7$\pm$2.8 mJy at 663 MHz). We detect linearly polarized radio emission associated with the `core' and the extended lobes of NGC 4235. Broadband polarimetric analysis yields an RM value of {$\sim200$ rad m$^{-2}$} in the `core', indicating Faraday rotation by magnetized plasma external to the synchrotron-emitting regions. Using these RM constraints, we estimate an average electron density of the Faraday-rotating medium of $\sim$3$\times10^{-2}$ cm$^{-3}$ for a characteristic perturbation scale of $\sim$0.3 parsec within an assumed magnetized region of size $\sim$1.3 kpc, consistent with a diffuse magnetized sheath or AGN-driven wind. These results extend classical Faraday rotation diagnostics to the low-power, radio-quiet AGN regime and demonstrate the potential of uGMRT broadband polarimetry for probing magnetized environments in and around such AGN.
reference: Salmoli Ghosh, Preeti Kharb, Janhavi Baghel (2026), arXiv:2610.10726.

title: Prevalence of radio Active Galactic Nuclei in galaxy groups since z=3.5 in the COSMOS-Web field
abstract: Radio active galactic nuclei (AGN) are key tracers of kinetic feedback from supermassive black holes. Although the dependence of their triggering on host stellar mass is well known, the impact of the large-scale environment across cosmic time is poorly understood. We investigate the role of the environment in triggering radio AGN activity, while also studying the dependence on stellar mass ($10\leq\log M_{\ast}\,{\rm [M_{\odot}]}\leq11.4$), radio luminosity ($22\leq\log L_{1.4}\,{\rm [W\,Hz^{-1}]}\leq26$), and redshift ($0.1\leq z \leq 3.5$). We combine the VLA-COSMOS 3 GHz Large Project with the COSMOS-Web galaxy and group catalogs, selecting radio-excess AGN and building radio luminosity functions (RLF) and radio AGN fractions separately for sources in galaxy groups (124 radio AGN) and in the field (405 radio AGN), out of the total of 20203 galaxies and 1678 galaxy groups. We fit the RLF to derive the cosmic evolution of radio AGN in different environments, and we provide a new parametric description of the radio AGN fractions as a function of environment, $M_{\ast}$, $L_{1.4}$, and z. Besides confirming the known positive correlation of radio AGN fraction with host $M_{\ast}$ in both groups and in the field, more importantly we find that the activation of a radio AGN in groups is enhanced relative to the field by a factor of 3--30 in space density and of 2 in radio AGN fraction at fixed stellar mass; the enhancement is also a function of $M_{\ast}$, $L_{1.4}$, and z. Furthermore, in all z bins, the radio AGN fractions peak within $r \leq 0.2R_{200}$. Overall, dense environments enhance radio AGN triggering out to at least z=3.5. We suggest the existence of a possible transition in the dominant triggering mechanism of radio AGN activity around z~1.5, potentially related to the intragroup medium in the core of groups at lower z and to merger and structure growth at earlier cosmic times.
reference: F. Ubertosi, I. Delvecchio, I. Prandoni et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.10719.

title: NGC 4936: abundant multi-phase medium in the central weak X-ray cool core and optically dark H I clouds in the group
abstract: We present a multiwavelength analysis of NGC 4936, the central galaxy of a weak cool-core group hosting an unusually large cold/warm gas reservoir. NGC 4936 contains $\sim2\times10^8$ M$_\odot$ of molecular gas in a rotating disk of radius $\sim1$ kpc, but no detected H I, with a $3σ$ upper limit of $1.13\times10^7$ M$_\odot$ within $\sim2.5$ kpc. The resulting $H_2$/H I mass ratio $>17$ is consistent with a predominantly molecular medium in the high-pressure environments of central galaxies. SOAR imaging and MUSE spectroscopy reveal ionised gas extending to $\sim15$ kpc in a complex filamentary morphology that broadly follows the molecular gas kinematics while extending well beyond the CO disk. Dust filaments similarly extend to $\sim14$ kpc and appear to interact with a companion galaxy located only $\sim2.5$ kpc away in projection. NGC 4936 has a star formation rate of $0.29$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$, and its AGN shows sub-mm and X-ray variability. We favour atmospheric condensation as the primary origin of the molecular gas, although externally acquired gas may contribute. Our recalculated thermodynamic profiles reach $t_{\rm cool}/t_{\rm ff}\sim25$ in the innermost region, placing the system near the threshold for multiphase condensation. The ongoing interaction may perturb the atmosphere and promote condensation while shaping the morphology and kinematics of the multiphase medium, rather than directly supplying most of the central cold gas. We additionally detect 20 H I structures in the surrounding group environment, with masses of $\sim10^7$--$10^8$ M$_\odot$, including several with no obvious optical counterparts.
reference: Prathamesh Tamhane, Ming Sun, Hao Chen et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.10721.

title: Accreting Neutron Stars in Low-Mass X-ray Binaries
abstract: Neutron star low-mass X-ray binaries (NS LMXBs) are systems in which a neutron star accretes matter from a Roche-lobe-filling companion via an accretion disc, releasing gravitational energy with an efficiency of order 10-20% of the rest-mass energy. Unlike black holes, neutron stars possess a solid surface and a magnetic field, making NS LMXBs uniquely rich laboratories for high-energy astrophysics and dense-matter physics. In this chapter we review the current understanding of accretion onto neutron stars in LMXBs, tracing matter from the outer disc radii to the stellar surface across five decades of observational discovery. We survey the principal classes of accreting neutron star systems - canonical atoll and Z-sources, ultracompact X-ray binaries, accreting millisecond pulsars, and transitional millisecond pulsars - and discuss how their spectral states, timing properties, and multiwavelength behaviour encode the physics of the inner accretion flow. We examine thermonuclear Type-I X-ray bursts as probes of nuclear burning and neutron star structure, and review the boundary and spreading layers where accreted matter decelerates onto the stellar surface. We discuss relativistic jets and ionised disc winds as regulators of the accretion-ejection cycle. Finally, we present X-ray polarimetric results from the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE), which for the first time provide new, though model-dependent, constraints on the geometry of the emission regions - disc, corona, spreading layer, and jets - that spectroscopy alone cannot resolve, alongside complementary optical and infrared polarimetric observations.
reference: M. C. Baglio, S. E. Motta, A. P. Nitindala et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.10691.

title: Discovery of a Nearby Ultra-fast Magnetic White Dwarf Propeller: Common Pathways to Magnetic Cataclysmic Variables
abstract: The fastest spinning white dwarfs (WDs), which approach break-up speeds, are found in close binary systems. In the two known magnetic WD ``propellers'', AE~Aqr and LAMOST J0240+1952, the magnetic WD spins so rapidly that it ejects the material transferred by its Roche-lobe-filling companion rather than accreting it. We report the discovery of the third such system, 1eRASS J042633.5$-$250226 (1eRASS J0426/Valeria), at only 265 pc, identified by combining SRG/eROSITA and \textit{Gaia} data via the ``X-ray Main Sequence''. TESS photometry shows AE~Aqr-like flaring and orbital modulation with $P_{\mathrm{orb}} \approx 6.62$ hr, and ZTF shows month-long high/low state changes. Phase-resolved Palomar/DBSP spectroscopy confirms the orbital period and yields a donor radial velocity of $K_2 = 202\pm7$ km s$^{-1}$. High-speed Palomar/CHIMERA photometry detects optical pulsations on three nights with the strongest detection at $P_\textrm{spin} = 26.8$ sec, though further observations are needed to confirm this as the WD spin. Spectral fitting of the donor in the low state reveals a late K-type star with $T_{\mathrm{donor}} = 4100\pm150$ K. Zeeman splitting in the optical spectrum yields a candidate field strength of $B_{\mathrm{WD}} = 26 \pm 3$ MG, meaning the system will evolve into a polar. Like other WD propellers, the system is X-ray faint ($L_X \approx 7\times 10^{30}$ erg s$^{-1}$), but is not detected in the radio, and a spin period is not detected in X-rays by SRG/eROSITA. The proximity of this system and evolutionary model constraints on the timeframe of the propeller phase yield a birth rate density of $\sim8\times10^{-16} \textrm{pc}^{-3} \textrm{yr}^{-1}$, which agrees with that of magnetic CVs, suggesting that a substantial fraction of magnetic CVs pass through a propeller phase.
reference: Antonio C. Rodriguez, Kareem El-Badry, R. Michael Rich et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.10689.

title: Deep Learning for Cherenkov Astronomy: Performance of GammaLearn on LST-1
authors: T. Vuillaume on behalf of the CTAO-LST Project
abstract: The Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) marks the next generation of Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACTs), offering a sensitivity improvement of up to a factor of 10 over current instruments. Its first prototype, the Large-Sized Telescope (LST-1), is already in operation at the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory in La Palma, Spain. Deep learning methods have shown significant promise in reconstructing key properties of incident particles, such as energy, arrival direction, and type, using simulated data. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on simplified image shape parameters, deep learning can exploit the full temporal and charge information of the recorded events, providing enhanced performance, particularly at low energies (~20 GeV) accessible by LST-1. This capability is especially valuable for observing distant extragalactic sources like Active Galactic Nuclei, which are key to probing fundamental physics and cosmology. In this work, by producing sensitivity curves, we evaluate the performance of GammaLearn, a deep learning framework tailored for IACT data analysis, by comparing it to the standard analysis used with LST-1 and applying it to real observational data from LST-1.
reference: G. Grolleron, C. Plard, M. Dell'aiera et al. (2026), arXiv:2610.10392.
